simple.meaning: אִישׁ (ʼîysh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a man as an individual or a male person; often used as an adjunct to a more definite term (and in such cases frequently not expressed in translation).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 2187 times across Genesis, beginning at Genesis 2:23. Its contexts include birth, family.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אִישׁ (H376).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: אִישׁ (ʼîysh) / H376 is traced through Genesis 2:23, Genesis 2:24, Genesis 3:6, Genesis 3:16 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.short: a man as an individual or a male person; often used as an adjunct to a more definite term (and in such cases frequently not expressed in translation)
